Title: should I master one language or should I learn multiple?
Body Information:
"Jack of all trades is a master of none but oftentimes better than a master of one" - That's why I mastered one language for the back-end and one for the front-end.

That said. C# and Java are general purpose languages that will allow you to write anything, and mastering just one of them will take a decade. For example I deal with C# and I'm currently learning .NET MAUI for mobile development, ASP .NET Core for API development and Blazor for front end. (I already know WPF)

Title: should I master one language or should I learn multiple?
Body Information: Stick to what you know, and learn more from it as much as possible. Those skills you learned will always be transferable to the others, esp web apps. After that it will be ez pizzy when learning new technologies, plus it is bad to learn all technologies at once, it will overwhelm you.

Title: Choosing Between NestJS and .NET for Long-Term Viability
Body Information: I would pick .NET, but many will see otherwise as this question depends on opinion, location and more. My view of it is that major companies generally go for mature solutions like Spring and .NET because of their legacy and already proven use in major companies, while I never used NestJS, I had friends who had very positive opinions about it, but it is still a very young technology and companies maybe reluctant to use it, plus the JS/TS backend ecosystem changes from one tech to another really fast so .NET is more time proof and even if it becomes obsolete I still think it gives you transferable knowledge that will aid you learn whatever the trend is 5-10 years later.
